title: Hunts FH-002S: A capped check-in code admits two members at its last unit

source.ref: Split from FH-002 (2026-11-16): the last-unit scarcity race was reproduced; the legacy cap is not atomic.

detail: A node with max_claims set (first N win, ADR-112) is enforced by a count in lib/engagement/verify.ts and a later insert in lib/engagement/capture.ts. Nothing holds the node between the two and each member has a different ledger key, so two members who scan together at the last unit both pass the count: two capture rows, two ledger rows, two Zap awards against a cap of one. A member arriving after them is refused, so the cap only fails inside the window. scripts/probes/hunts/legacy-seams.mjs reproduces it with the shipped orchestrators against the in-memory fixture (no database was raced). Owed, by Engagement with the owner's call on which: make the cap atomic (one database function that locks the node, counts and inserts, or a constraint the insert can fail on) or retire max_claims in favour of Hunt reward stock (hunt_reward_grant already serialises on the reward row). Still unproven anywhere in CI: two live Postgres sessions racing hunt_reward_grant; supabase/tests/hunt_rewards.test.sql covers the sequential last unit and records a by-hand two-session check. Done when: two members competing for the last unit leave one capture and one award, and the probe passes. Requires: FH-002. Owner role: Engagement.
